observations: A disposable non-root Linux environment inside Docker Desktop exercised the frozen source with Claude Code 2.1.273 and Bedrock authentication; credentials remained external to the fixture.
Installation, adoption, repeat sync, drift and conflict detection, uninstall restoration, and preservation of unrelated user configuration and skills completed in the isolated home.

Native responses changed from PLAIN to TAGGED after switching one custom proof-label stance. Session and project overrides and the built-in delegation and voice stances resolved through the same shared primitive authority.

Manual mode and an autonomy denial prevented disposable writes, while an explicitly acknowledged bypass created its sentinel. Claude Code 2.1.273 requires Sonnet 5 for native Auto Mode; the tested Bedrock account has zero Sonnet 5 runtime quota, so the Auto selection remained unavailable and created no write without weakening native restrictions.

Native lifecycle execution produced both per-path Review Card results for a multi-file operation and retained an independent user hook. Constrained gatherer and planner workers completed, and their forced project writes were denied.
Stop-gate runs covered unchanged, staged, untracked, edited-untracked, failure, and retry-budget states. The full four-layer BMad review completed and preserved the implementation bytes.
A Claude to Codex to Claude handoff advanced three revisions, rejected stale state, demoted inherited verification, and transferred no approvals.
